newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Ukraine president hopes for stability in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine president hopes for stability in Russia.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, on a visit to Lithuania, said on Tuesday he hoped Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health problems would not plunge Russia into instability.
"I believe that we (Ukraine and Lithuania) have one common problem: we both want stability in Russia," Kuchma told a news conference at the end of a two-day trip to the Baltic state.
"We wish Russia to pass through this period of indecision, brought on by President's Yeltsin's health, as quickly as possible."

Yeltsin has been in hospital for more than a week. But a top Russian surgeon who suggested at the weekend that a bypass operation on the president could be postponed or cancelled said on Tuesday there was no chance of cancelling the surgery.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin ruled out any suggestion that Yeltsin would step down as demanded by his communist rivals.
Relations between Ukraine and Russia were not easy after the collapse in 1991 of the former Soviet Union but Kuchma has overseen an improvement in ties since his election in 1994.

He backed Yeltsin's re-election bid in July but relations are dogged by disagreement over the Black Sea Fleet. The two sides have agreed on splitting the 900 ships but are divided over bases in Crimea, where mainly ethnic Russians live.

In Lithuania, Kuchma restated his support for all three Baltic states -- including Latvia and Estonia -- to join NATO. Ukraine says it has no immediate plans to join the Alliance but rejects the notion of any state vetoing membership for former Communist states.
Russia vehemently opposes NATO's plans and is particularly sensitive about the idea of including former Soviet republics in its expansion eastwards.
